name: Chateau de Blois, Francois I wing

dates.altered: The Inventaire notice lists construction campaigns running to 1845 and 1868 and names Félix Duban, Anatole de Baudot, Jules Grenouillot and Jules de La Morandière among the authors: the wing a visitor sees is a nineteenth-century restoration of a sixteenth-century fabric.
dates.note: The node's exemplar dates the François I wing 1515-1524, and the Inventaire notice's campaign list '1498 ; 1508 ; 1515 ; 1524 ; 1635 ; 1638 ; 1845 ; 1868' contains both those years - the one figure in this cluster where the register corroborates the corpus exactly. The protection notice PA00098337 gives only '16e siècle ; 17e siècle' for the whole castle.

refs.title: Château - POP
refs.note: The Inventaire général notice for the same castle, and the richer of the two; it is the survey block below. Its 'Commentaire concernant la datation' reads 'daté par source ; daté par travaux historiques', which is the register saying how it knows.

survey.prepared: The notice prints 'Rédacteur de la notice Cosperec Annie' and is signed '© Inventaire général'.

measurements.name: francois_i_campaign_start_year
measurements.note: A year, not a dimension. Carried because it is the register's own corroboration of the node's date for this wing; `count` is the nearest unit the closed enum offers. The notice lists eight campaign years and does not say which belongs to which wing - reading 1515 and 1524 as the François I wing is this record's inference from the node, not the register's statement.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. THE EXEMPLAR NAMES A WING AND THE REGISTER LISTS A CASTLE. Neither Mérimée notice describes the François I wing separately; both describe the whole royal château, whose four ranges span the thirteenth to the seventeenth century and were restored in the nineteenth. The record is therefore about the castle and says so, rather than pretending a notice about the whole is a notice about the part. No rights line was read, so no `rights_evidence`.
